modes.title: Remove Glare
modes.subtitle: Erase reflections, glare and light spots from lenses
modes.prompt: Edit only the reflections on the lenses of the glasses in this photo. First judge how see-through the lenses are in the original photo, then follow the matching rule. Clear or lightly tinted lenses (eyes already visible behind them): remove every reflection, glare, light spot, highlight, sparkle and window, screen, lamp or sky reflection so the lenses look clean and see-through, and restore the eyes behind them realistically, keeping the person's exact eye shape, eye color, iris and pupil size, gaze direction, eyelids, eyelashes, skin tone and the original lighting. Dark, opaque or mirrored sunglasses (eyes not visible in the original): remove only the glare, light spots and reflected scenes, and keep the lenses exactly as dark and opaque as they are, as a smooth, even surface with the original tint, color, gradient and finish. Do not add, draw, invent or reveal eyes, do not make the lenses transparent, lighter or see-through. Gradient lenses: apply the clear-lens rule only where the eyes are already visible and the sunglasses rule where the lens is dark. Never invent eye details that cannot be seen in the original photo. Keep the lens tint, color, darkness and natural optical distortion unchanged. Do not modify the glasses frame, nose pads or temples in any way. Do not change the face, facial features, identity, expression, skin, makeup, hair, clothing, body, pose, background, colors, white balance, contrast, sharpness, grain, resolution, aspect ratio, crop or framing. Do not retouch, beautify, smooth, relight or enhance anything. Everything outside the lens area must remain pixel-identical to the original photo. Output the same photo with only the lens reflections removed.

modes.title: Remove Glasses
modes.subtitle: Take the glasses off entirely, naturally
modes.prompt: Edit only the eyeglasses in this photo. Completely remove the glasses from the person's face, including the frame, lenses, nose pads, hinges and temple arms, and any part of the temples over the ears or hair. Reconstruct the areas that were covered or distorted by the glasses so the person looks exactly as they would without glasses: their real eyes, eyebrows, eyelids, eyelashes, under-eye area, nose bridge, cheeks, temples, ears and hair, with the same identity, eye shape, eye color, gaze direction, skin tone, skin texture and pores, and lighting as the rest of the face. Remove the lens magnification or shrinking effect so the eyes have their natural size and position. Remove nose pad marks, frame shadows and lens reflections. Do not change the face shape, facial features, identity, age, expression, makeup, hair style, clothing, body, pose, background, colors, white balance, contrast, sharpness, grain, resolution, aspect ratio, crop or framing. Do not retouch, beautify, smooth, relight or enhance anything. Everything not covered by the glasses must remain pixel-identical to the original photo. Output the same photo with only the glasses removed.
